title: I am trying to verify my domain with Google Workspace. I need to add a TXT record to my domains DNS settings. I have confirmed that my domain is connected to Wix via pointing. What to do now?
content:
Q: I am trying to verify my domain with Google Workspace. I need to add a TXT record to my domains DNS settings. I have confirmed that my domain is connected to Wix via pointing. What to do now?
A: To verify your domain with Google Workspace by adding a TXT record, you need to manage your DNS settings with your domain host, not Wix, since your domain is connected via pointing. Follow these steps:

1. Log in to your domain host account where your DNS records are managed.
2. Add the TXT record provided by Google Workspace to your domain's DNS settings.
3. After adding the TXT record, return to the Google Admin Console and click 'Verify'.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/manually-verifying-your-domain-with-google-workspace-formerly-g-suite

title: I want to know more about the "Right Click Protect App" to prevent visitors from copying my website content.
content:
Q: I want to know more about the "Right Click Protect App" to prevent visitors from copying my website content.
A: The Right Click Protect app is a tool available from the Wix App Market designed to help prevent visitors from downloading images or copying text from your website by displaying a custom copyright message when they attempt to right-click. However, it does not prevent copying via Ctrl+C or using the print screen function. 
To add the app, you can go to your Wix Editor, click on 'Add Apps', search for the Right Click Protect app, and add it to your site. 
You can customize the message that appears when someone right-clicks on your content.

I have purchased the new domain but havent added it to my Wix account yet. I need to know if my current subscription can be easily changed to the new domain once I set it up on Wix.

If you want to connect a domain you already own to your Wix account, we strongly recommend doing so by changing its name servers.

Go to Premium Subscriptions in your Wix account.
Click the More Actions icon next to the plan you wish to reassign.

title: I'm a sole trader in the UK. What account type is best for me?
content:
Q: I'm a sole trader in the UK. What account type is best for me?
A: UK sole proprietors are required to submit a Unique Taxpayer Reference (UTR) number as well as a business bank account when setting up their Wix Payments account.
If you haven't registered for a UTR, or possess only a personal bank account, you can choose an Individual account instead.

title: What are the collection limits in Wix Store?
content:
Q: What are the collection limits in Wix Store?
A: To ensure that the Wix Stores platform remains stable and that your online store is usable and fast, Wix has set the following limitations:
  
  - Products: You can upload up to 50,000 products from the Wix Stores Dashboard manually or by CSV import.
  - Product Options per Product: Each product can have up to 6 product options (e.g. color, size, material).
  - Choices per Product Option: Each product option (e.g. size) can have up to 100 option choices (e.g. Green, Blue)
  - Product Variants: You can create up to 1,000 variants per product.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-stores-limits-recommended-guidelines

It may take up to 3-5 business days for the funds to reach your bank account after being processed, depending on your financial institution.

Q: My banking information for payouts hasnt been updated for a couple of weeks. I need help with identifying if theres an issue with the verification process for my individual account or if the details were not updated correctly.

In addition to meeting the requirements below, the verification process begins once you've accepted the first successful payment to your Wix Payments account.

Depending on your account type, review the relevant checklist to make sure you're providing the requested information correctly: 
Individual account
Make sure you've written your personal information correctly:
Your first / middle / last name and your date of birth must match those listed in your photo ID. 
Double check that you've entered your bank account number(s) correctly.
Enter a physical address to verify your account. PO Boxes are not accepted as a valid address. 
Upload an address verification document, such as a utility bill, to confirm your address. The document must have been issued within the last 6 months.
Add your Business Description:
Enter your Doing Business As name (The operating name of your business)
Use the dropdown menu to select your Business Type
Use the text box to add a short description of your products / services
Upload a color copy of your photo ID and a bank statement to verify your identity.

Allow 7 business days for the account to be verified. If 7 business days have already passed and you've verified the information is correct and matches your bank account details, contact Wix Customer Care. We will be happy to investigate this issue further.

title: How can I set up a flat rate shipping fee in Wix Stores.
content:
Q: How can I set up a flat rate shipping fee in Wix Stores.
A: To set up flat rate shipping and charge the same rate for all purchases delivered to a certain region, please follow these steps:

Step 1 | Create or Select a Shipping Region

 A region can be made of one or more countries. Alternatively, it can be made of one or more regions within a country. You can set up different shipping regions for your store. For example, a merchant might set up 4 shipping rules: a local shipping region for California, a region for the rest of the US, another for Mexico and Canada, and finally one for the rest of the world.
Important:
If there is no rule for a region, customers from that region cannot make store purchases.
If you previously set up shipping (and tax) in a merchant account (e.g. in PayPal), remove these settings before starting.

1. Go to the Shipping & fulfillment settings in your site's dashboard.
2. Select an option:
- Edit a default rule: Click the region you want to set up.
- Create a new rule:
a. Click Add Region.
b. Click +Add destination, start typing a country name and select it. 
3. Click Done or move directly on to the next step.

Step 2 | Set Up a Flat Rate Shipping Rule
1. Select Flat Rate from the Select how shipping is calculated drop-down.
2. Enter a name in the Shipping Option Name field (e.g. Standard Shipping).
3. Enter the shipping rate.
4. Click the Offer Free Shipping when customer buys over a certain amount checkbox and enter the amount.
Note: If you create additional shipping services (e.g. priority shipping), this checkbox must be selected and the amount specified to apply to each rule.
5. Click Add another Delivery Option to add an additional options (e.g. Express Shipping).
6. Click Save.

Step 3 | Offer Local Delivery or Pickup options
After saving your shipping rule, you can select the region again and add local delivery or pickup options.

title: how long does it take for my website to go live/be accessible?
content:
Q: how long does it take for my website to go live/be accessible?
A: Once you publish your Wix site, it typically goes live immediately. However, if you've connected a custom domain, it may take up to 48 hours for domain propagation to complete. During this time, your site might not be accessible from all devices or may appear as insecure.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/about-domain-propagation
evidence_json:
["About Domain Propagation
https://support.wix.com/en/article/about-domain-propagation
About Domain Propagation
A domain's DNS (Domain Name System) converts web URLs (such as www.wix.com) into IP addresses (a combination of numbers read by a computer), which is used to exchange data across the internet. DNS matches names with numbers to deliver websites to your browser. Domain propagation is the process of updating name servers around the world following any changes to your DNS records. It can take up to 48 hours to complete. This means that your site may not be accessible from all devices, or may appear as insecure during this time. As soon as propagation is complete, your site will be accessible and secure worldwide.Important:Domain propagation may take up to 48 hours to complete.During the domain propagation process:You may not be able to view your live site online. Your previously connected live site may appear on your domain. You may not receive emails connected to your domain. Published changes to your site may not appear on your live site. Your site may appear correctly in one browser or computer, but not in another. The SSL certificate will only be issued once propagation is "]

title: What's the difference between 'site sessions' and 'unique visitors'?
content:
Q: What's the difference between 'site sessions' and 'unique visitors'?
A: Site sessions' refer to visits to your site, starting when a visitor arrives and ending after a period of inactivity. Multiple page views and actions can occur within a single session. 'Unique visitors' are individual people who visit your site, counted uniquely by device and browser. If the same person visits from different devices, they are counted as separate unique visitors.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-analytics-traffic-sales-and-behavior-overviews

title: What stages does a customer payment go through before it reaches my bank account with Wix Payments?
content:
Q: What stages does a customer payment go through before it reaches my bank account with Wix Payments?
A: Each payment from your customer goes through 3 stages before it reaches your bank account with Wix Payments:

1. **Processing Payment:** After your customer makes a successful payment, the payment is processed. Processing usually takes 2-5 business days and involves two parts happening simultaneously:
   - The settlement period, which generally takes 1-2 days but can be longer depending on the customer’s payment method.
   - The pending period, lasting between 2-5 business days, is in place to protect against fraudulent activity.

2. **Scheduled Payout:** The payment is added to your next scheduled daily, weekly, or monthly payout. If you have multiple payment methods active in Wix Payments, your payouts may be grouped by payment method.

3. **Sent Payout:** The payout is sent from Wix Payments and typically arrives in your bank account within 3-5 business days, with various factors like weekdays, currency, or bank holidays affecting the arrival date of your payout.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/receiving-your-payouts-from-wix-payments

["Receiving Your Payouts from Wix Payments
https://support.wix.com/en/article/receiving-your-payouts-from-wix-payments
Receiving Your Payouts from Wix Payments

title: How can I set up a tax group for products with special tax rates in Wix Restaurants Orders (New)?
content:
Q: How can I set up a tax group for products with special tax rates in Wix Restaurants Orders (New)?
A: To set up a tax group for products with special tax rates in Wix Restaurants Orders (New), follow these steps:

1. **Determine which items have special tax rates**: First, identify which items are taxed at rates different from the general sales tax rate. You should consult with an accountant or your local tax authority to determine the correct rates.

2. **Create a tax group**: Navigate to the **Tax** section in your site's dashboard and scroll down to **Tax groups**. Click **+Add Group**, enter a group name (e.g., "Car Seats"), and click **Add**. Note that the tax group name is not visible to customers, so choose a name that helps you remember its purpose.

3. **Assign your group's tax rates**: For each tax location where you do business, select the location and enter the appropriate tax rate for your group. Go to **Tax** in your site's dashboard, select a location, enter the tax rate for the group you created, and click **Save**. Repeat for any other locations. If you don't enter a rate for a location, items in the tax group will be taxed at 0% in that location.

4. **Add items to the group**: After setting up your tax groups, assign items to them:
   - For adding multiple products at once, go to **Tax** in your site's dashboard, hover over the relevant tax group, click **Add Products**, select your products, and click **Save**.
   - For adding a single product, go to **Products** in your site's dashboard, select the product, and choose the relevant tax group from the **Product tax group** drop-down.

   For restaurant menu items, go to **Menus (New)** in your site's dashboard, select the menu item, click the **Ordering tab**, and select the relevant tax group from the **Items tax group** drop-down (e.g., "Alcoholic Beverages").

If you're using Avalara automatic tax calculation, Avalara will automatically assign the correct tax setting for each location you have added when creating tax groups.

title: What are the best practices for choosing an image for a social media post?
content:
Q: What are the best practices for choosing an image for a social media post?
A: When choosing an image for a social media post, follow these best practices:

- **Use high resolution images:** Ensure you're using an image with the best resolution possible. The clearer the image, the more professional your post looks. Choose an image that clearly shows the point of the post so that someone viewing it on their social media feed immediately understands its purpose.

- **Don't add too much text to the image:** Avoid distracting or crowding the image with text. Stick to the '20% Rule': Facebook research found that images with less than 20% of text got more attention and performed better. For example, if you're posting about a limited time sale, your image text could say "50% off site wide for 2 days only." Use the caption to add more text and detail.

For more detailed guidelines, you can refer to the [image formatting guidelines](https://support.wix.com/en/article/social-media-marketing-best-practices-for-writing-social-posts).

A: When printing your logo, the ideal file type to use is an SVG file. An SVG file is an infinitely scalable file that doesn't decrease in quality; no matter how much you expand or shrink it. Since SVG logo files are infinitely scalable, you can use them for any kind of purpose – from mini-magazine ads, up to huge billboards.

title: How can I customize the design of my event schedule page in Wix?
content:
Q: How can I customize the design of my event schedule page in Wix?
A: Prerequisites: Create an event schedule.

To customize the design of your event schedule page in Wix, follow these steps:

1. **Access the Event Schedule**
   - **Wix Editor**
     1. Click **Pages** on the left side of the Editor.
     2. Click **Event Pages**.
     3. Select **Schedule**.
   - **Editor X**
     1. Click the **Pages** icon at the top bar of Editor X.
     2. Scroll down and select **Schedule**.

2. **Customize the Schedule Design**

title: What are the keyboard shortcuts for managing elements in the Wix Editor?
content:
Q: What are the keyboard shortcuts for managing elements in the Wix Editor?
A: In the Wix Editor, you can use the following keyboard shortcuts to manage elements:

- **Ctrl + X**: Cut
- **Ctrl + C**: Copy
- **Ctrl + V**: Paste
- **Ctrl + D**: Duplicate
- **Delete Backspace**: Delete an element
- **Ctrl + ↓**: Move backward
- **Ctrl + ↑**: Move forward
- **Ctrl + Shift + ↓**: Send to back
- **Ctrl + Shift + ↑**: Bring to front
- **←, ↑, →, ↓**: Move single pixel (i.e. Nudge)
- **Shift + ↑, ↓**: Move 10 pixels
- **Ctrl + Z**: Undo
- **Ctrl + Y**: Redo
- **Ctrl + Shift + M**: Select next element
- **Ctrl + M**: Select previous element
- **Ctrl + click element**: Direct element selection (select elements, skipping the section/strip/container they're attached to)
- **Shift + click element**: Select multiple elements
- **Hold Shift while rotating element**: Rotates element in 15° increments
- **Hold Shift while dragging element**: Keeps element aligned on the same x or y axis
- **Alt + Drag**: Duplicate and drag the new element
- **Esc during Drag, Resize or Rotate**: Cancels the action
- **Shift + Tab**: Navigates between elements
- **Enter while on an element**: Triggers the element's main action
- **Shift + 1/2/3**: Opens the element's panels (Settings, Layouts, Design)
- **Ctrl + mouse click elements in Add panel**: Keeps Add panel open

For Mac users, use the **Command** ⌘ key instead of the **Ctrl** key, and the **Option** key instead of the **Alt** key.

title: Why won't videos autoplay on my website when using certain browsers?

content:
Q: What should I do if I receive a 'Couldn't Fetch' error for my sitemap in Google Search Console?
A: If you receive a "Couldn't Fetch" error in the Status field for your sitemap, first check to see that the URL path in the sitemap field on the left says "/sitemap.xml" and not the page URL (e.g., "/homepage"). If it was submitted incorrectly, go ahead and submit it again. If the sitemap URL is correct, note that this error is known to occur for sites hosted with any company and is not related to Wix. In most cases, it resolves itself within a couple of days or weeks. However, you can submit the URL using the Inspection Tool to speed up the process.

title: What are role addresses and how do they affect email deliverability?
content:
Q: What are role addresses and how do they affect email deliverability?
A: Role addresses are **organizational email addresses that represent a function or responsibility rather than an individual.** They are most likely managed by more than one person and represent multiple recipients who handle the incoming emails. The most common examples of role addresses include info@, support@, and billing@. 

While role addresses are a helpful tool for larger companies, **they should not be used for personal use and we recommend that you do not send campaigns to them.** Because role addresses are often associated with many recipients (such as a business's 'support@' redirecting to 20 customer service representatives), they can generate spam complaints or fall into spam traps. 

Some other issues with role addresses and email deliverability include: 
* **High bounce rates:** Since role addresses represent a distribution list (being sent to more than one person) there's a high chance that one of those addresses on the list is no longer valid or doesn't exist, causing it to bounce.
* **Possible blacklist:** There are many sign ups that don't allow role addresses, because if someone on that distribution list reports your email as spam, it could get you on a blacklist.
* **Compliance issues:** It's highly unlikely that every recipient in a role based email addresses gave their consent to receive your email. Also, email marketing best practices recommend the 'double opt-in' strategy which means someone has to confirm their email to be added to a subscription list. Double opt-in won't work with role addresses.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/about-role-addresses
evidence_json:
["About Role Addresses
https://support.wix.com/en/article/about-role-addresses
About Role Addresses
You've most likely sent an email to a role address (or role-based-address) without realizing it. Info@, contact@, support@ are all examples of role addresses that are common in businesses to help them stay organized. However, using a role address can have a negative impact on your email deliverability.In this article:
What are role addresses? Common types of role addresses How role addresses affect your email deliverabilityWhat Are Role Addresses?Role addresses are organizational email addresses that represent a function or responsibility rather than an individual. They are most likely managed by more than one person and represent multiple recipients who handle the incoming emails. title: What are the guidelines for creating a user name in Google Workspace?
content:
Q: What are the guidelines for creating a user name in Google Workspace?
A: To create a user name in Google Workspace, follow these guidelines:

- User names can be between 1 and 64 characters in length.
- User names may contain any of the following: letters (a - z), numbers (0 - 9), dashes (-), underscores (_), apostrophes ('), and periods (.).
- User names may **not** contain any of the following: ampersands (&), equal signs (=), brackets (< >), plus signs (+), commas (,), or more than one period (.) in a row.
- User names may **not** begin or end with a period (.), nor can a period (.) be the only character.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/google-workspace-username-and-password-guidelines

["Google Workspace: Username and Password Guidelines
https://support.wix.com/en/article/google-workspace-username-and-password-guidelines

When purchasing a Google Workspace business email, you are required to choose a user name and password (or multiple if you have multiple users). User names and passwords must match the conventions set by Google. To make sure that your user name and password are accepted, follow the guidelines below.User NameUser names can be between 1 and 64 characters in length.User names may contain any of the following; letters (a - z), numbers (0 - 9), dashes (-), underscores (_), apostrophes ('), and periods (.).User names may not contain any of the following; ampersands (&), equal signs (=), brackets (< >), plus signs (+), commas (,), or more than one period (.) in a row.User names may not begin or end with a period (.), nor can a period (.) be the only character.PasswordPasswords must be made up of English ASCII characters only.Passwords must be between 8 and 100 characters in length."]

title: How does Wix use IndexNow to inform search engines about changes to my site?
content:
Q: How does Wix use IndexNow to inform search engines about changes to my site?
A: Wix uses IndexNow to instantly alert search engines, like Bing and Yandex, about any changes made on your website, making crawling more efficient. The IndexNow functionality is included with your Premium plan. Wix checks when there are changes to your site pages and submits the changes on your behalf to the IndexNow protocol. This allows search engines to quickly identify that a page was changed and reflect the change in search results. Normally, it can take time for search engines to crawl and index your site, but with a Premium site, Wix automatically makes IndexNow aware of any site changes without you having to keep on top of it. For example, if you add a new blog post to your site, Wix notifies IndexNow, and IndexNow then pings relevant search engines about the changes. This allows the search engines to crawl and index the page faster (depending on their indexing factors).

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/how-wix-uses-indexnow-to-inform-search-engines-about-your-site-changes
evidence_json:
["How Wix Uses IndexNow to Inform Search Engines About Your Site Changes
https://support.wix.com/en/article/how-wix-uses-indexnow-to-inform-search-engines-about-your-site-changes
How Wix Uses IndexNow to Inform Search Engines About Your Site Changes
Before you begin:IndexNow with Wix is only available for sites with a Premium plan.IndexNow is a way to instantly alert search engines, like Bing and Yandex, about any changes made on your website, making crawling more efficient. The IndexNow functionality is included with your Premium plan. Wix checks when there are changes to your site pages. We then submit the changes on your behalf to the IndexNow protocol. What is IndexNow?The IndexNow protocol makes the process of search engines crawling your site and indexing them more efficient. IndexNow explains its functionality as "a simple ping so that search engines know that a URL and its content has been added, updated, or deleted." This allows search engines to quickly identify that a page was changed and reflect the change in search results. Without IndexNow, it can take anywhere from hours to months for changes to be discovered by search engines.Tip:Read more about Wix SEO's IndexNow int"]

title: How can I customize text carried over from the desktop version in the Wix mobile editor?
content:
Q: How can I customize text carried over from the desktop version in the Wix mobile editor?
A: To customize text carried over from the desktop version in the Wix mobile editor, follow these steps:

1. Click the text element in the mobile editor.
2. Customize the text by doing the following:

### Adjust text size
To increase or decrease your text size, click the Scale Up or Scale Down icons.

**Tip:** You can also change the size of your text by clicking the Settings icon and dragging the **Font Size** slider accordingly.

### Change the text's color and alignment
1. Click the **Settings** icon.
2. Customize the following:
   * **Color:** Click the color box and choose your new color from the Color Picker.
   * **Alignment:** Choose how your text is aligned (left, centered, right, justified).

### Enable vertical text
1. Click the **Settings** icon.
2. Click the **Enable Vertical Text** toggle to change your text from horizontal to vertical for languages with a vertical writing system (e.g. Japanese).

### Resize button text
Click the **Scale Up** or **Scale Down** icons to make the text bigger or smaller.

title: What are the product limits in Wix Stores and what happens if I exceed them?

Q: What are the product limits in Wix Stores and what happens if I exceed them?
A: ### Wix Stores Platform Limits:
- **Products**: You can upload up to 50,000 products from the Wix Stores Dashboard manually or by CSV import.
- **Product Options per Product**: Each product can have up to 6 product options (e.g. color, size, material).
- **Choices per Product Option**: Each product option (e.g. size) can have up to 100 option choices (e.g. Green, Blue).
- **Product Variants**: You can create up to 1,000 variants per product.

### What happens if you exceed any of these limits?
When you approach or exceed a limit, you'll first receive a notification in the Wix Stores Dashboard. When you exceed one of these limits, you’ll receive an error message.

title: How can I enable or disable the autosave feature in the Wix Editor?
content:
Q: How can I enable or disable the autosave feature in the Wix Editor?
A: To enable or disable autosave in the Wix Editor, press **Ctrl** + **Alt** + **A** (Windows), or **Command** ⌘ + **Option** + **A** (Mac) on your keyboard.

### Notes
* There is no autosave for site collaborators.
* Adding apps to your site will trigger an automatic autosave, regardless of whether autosave has been disabled.
* Viewing your site Preview will trigger an automatic autosave, regardless of whether autosave has been disabled.

title: How does Wix's Smart Algorithm optimize Facebook ad campaigns?
content:
Q: How does Wix's Smart Algorithm optimize Facebook ad campaigns?
A: Wix's Smart Algorithm optimizes Facebook ad campaigns by using advanced data science algorithms and a lot of data. Here's how it works:

- **Audiences**: The decision-making engine creates more variations of Lookalikes, engagement, and remarketing audiences. It measures their potential reach and performance using data from the business’ Facebook Page, pixel, and campaign stats.

- **Targeting**: It takes users’ predefined targeting and breaks it down into age, gender, locations, interests, and placements in Facebook and Instagram. It measures the effectiveness of each and decides when to broaden the audience, break it down, or take no action. The best audiences with the highest potential for conversion are chosen, while low-quality audiences are paused.

- **Ad Sets**: The algorithm pauses ad sets with negative trends, low quality, low conversion rate, or low engagement rank. It resumes ad sets with new potential signals based on new engaging insights from the campaign or pixel.

The algorithm runs daily analyses of every change in campaign performance from Facebook and Instagram, combined with data from your website. It uses this data to run unique decision-making models and trend analyses, simulating and estimating the effectiveness of each action to fine-tune the campaign.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/facebook-ads-about-wixs-smart-algorithm
evidence_json:
["Facebook Ads: About Wix’s Smart Algorithm
https://support.wix.com/en/article/facebook-ads-about-wixs-smart-algorithm
Facebook Ads: About Wix’s Smart Algorithm
Billions of people use Facebook and Instagram every day, and 8 million businesses sell on those platforms, because they have a captive, engaged audience. But even with those opportunities comes the challenge of competing with bigger businesses with huge marketing budgets.Because of the large competition, the vast majority of businesses running Facebook ads themselves will fail as optimizing the campaign requires a lot of knowledge and time. For each ad, you compete with everybody on Facebook & Instagram. You need to be an expert in online marketing to be successful. That's why Wix came up with a solution.
Wix's AI Solution – Your Own Marketing GeniusRunning Facebook campaigns takes a lot of time and effort, and is very hard, so we decided to build an automatic one, using advance data science algorithms and a lot of data.After almost a year of tests and experiments, learning from millions of Wix users, our unique AI model was built and is now ready to fully manage your campaign like a marketing genius.The algorithm runs daily "]

title: Can I migrate my email data from an external email host to my Google Workspace account?
content:

title: How can I customize the settings of my gallery in ADI?
content:
Q: How can I customize the settings of my gallery in ADI?
A: Prerequisites: Ensure that you have added a gallery to your site and added media to it.

To customize your gallery settings:

1. Click your gallery in the ADI builder.
2. Customize your gallery settings on the panel on the left using the available options:
   
   * **Full Width:** Switch on the toggle to expand your gallery across the width of your site.
   * **Load More Button:** Switch on the toggle to show a 'Load More' button for galleries with more items than fit in the section layout.
   * **Image Ratio:** Select a ratio of the gallery items. The images automatically update on the page so you can see how it looks.
   * **When Clicking On an Item:** Click the drop-down to select what happens when visitors click a gallery item:
     
     + **A Link Opens:** Visitors are directed to a link (a web address, page, lightbox, etc.)
     
     **Note:** To set up a link click **Manage Media** beneath the drop-down.
     + **Nothing Happens:** Nothing happens when someone clicks an item.
     + **Open in Full Screen:** The gallery item expands in fullscreen mode so visitors can get a closer look.
   * **Display Elements:** Select the elements to include in the gallery alongside the gallery items.
     
     + **Image Title:** Display the title of the gallery item. **Note**: Click **Manage Media** at the bottom to update your titles.
     + **Image Description:** Include the description of the item. **Note**: Click **Manage Media** at the bottom to update the item description.
     + **Social Sharing:** Add social media icons to your gallery items so visitors can share the media.
     + **Download:** Add a download icon beside each gallery item so visitors can download your media.
     + **Heart Icon:** Add a heart icon so visitors can react to their favorite gallery items.
   * **Image Quality:** Drag the slider to change the image quality.
   * **Image Sharpening:** Select the checkmark to sharpen your image using the amount, radius and threshold controls.

**Note:** Some settings may be different or unavailable based on the gallery layout you choose.

title: How can I update the prices and availability for my rooms using Wix Hotels by HotelRunner?
content:
Q: How can I update the prices and availability for my rooms using Wix Hotels by HotelRunner?
A: To update the prices and availability for your rooms using Wix Hotels by HotelRunner, you can use the **Inventory Calendar** tab. Here, you can make changes to the availability and price rates for each of your rooms as required. You can filter the calendar view by Room type, Rate plan, or Channels.

For price or availability updates to multiple rooms at once, use the **Bulk Updates** tab. Here you can update your rooms, rate plans, and prices in bulk. Filter the view by Rate plan, by channel, or both.

Choose what you want to update from the following options:

* **Base Price:** Update base price rates for a given period of time. Choose between a fixed monetary adjustment or a percentage adjustment.
* **Availability:** Update how many rooms of a certain type you have available. Make sure this new number is accurate to avoid over-bookings.
* **Minimum stay:** Encourage longer stays by setting a minimum stay restriction. This is useful during high season.
* **Stop Sell:** Block the sale of certain rates for a period of time. This is useful during low seasons.
* **Closed to arrival:** Restrict guests from arriving on specific dates. This is useful during holidays to better manage your staff’s workload.
* **Closed to departure:** Restrict guests from departing on specific dates. This is useful to better manage your staff’s workload.

Then select the relevant start and end dates, and specific days of the week you want to update.

content:
Q: Why can't I access my free Wix site in Saudi Arabia?
A: We are aware that some users are experiencing issues when accessing free Wix sites in Saudi Arabia. title: Why does the amount on my Wix invoice differ from the amount on my bank statement?
content:
Q: Why does the amount on my Wix invoice differ from the amount on my bank statement?
A: There are two main reasons why the amount listed on your bank statement might not match the amount on your Wix invoice:

* **The amounts are in different currencies:** Depending on your location, the amount listed on your Wix invoice may be displayed in US dollars (for example, in Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Hong Kong, Argentina, Israel or Singapore). The amount you see on your bank statement will be in your local currency.

* **You have been charged bank fees:** Your bank may charge additional processing fees for your payment. For example, a transaction fee or a currency conversion fee.

**Note:** Bank fees or exchange rates are not determined or controlled by Wix.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/different-amount-appearing-on-your-wix-invoice-and-bank-statement

title: What proactive measures does Wix take to moderate content under the Digital Services Act?
content:
Q: What proactive measures does Wix take to moderate content under the Digital Services Act?
A: Wix undertakes voluntary investigations aiming to identify and act against illegal content by applying a combination of automated tools and human review to proactively moderate content on our platform. Our automated tools are designed to make our best efforts in trying to identify specific illegal activities, such as:

* **Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM):** Once identified, our team of trained moderators reviews and, if necessary, takes action on suspicious content.
* **Phishers and Fraudster Behaviour:** Based on specific patterns, we strive to identify accounts that have the primary purpose of conducting any form of web forgery. This includes publishing malicious websites or tricking visitors into giving up sensitive information such as passwords, account details, or credit card numbers.

title: What are some red flags to watch out for when accepting card payments to prevent fraud?
content:
Q: What are some red flags to watch out for when accepting card payments to prevent fraud?
A: To minimize risks and possible chargebacks while accepting online orders, be wary of the following potential red flags:

- **Bulk orders**: Large orders on goods that have high resale value (sneakers, electronics, designers’ handbags, etc). Large repeated orders on such items also pose a high risk.
- **Card processing behaviors:** Multiple lost or stolen declines, or multiple attempts from different cards. It is unlikely that one customer will have 6 or more cards. Likewise, beware of cases where customers ask to split the payment into 2 or more instalments, especially using different cards.
- **Unusual shipping behavior:** Be wary if shipping is overpriced in comparison to the value of goods; if your customer insists on a rush-shipping option without sign-on delivery; or shipping to forwarding companies that provide reshipping to "third countries".
- **3rd party payment requests**: Avoid requests to pay for special “vendor” services that you do not offer (such as door-to-door delivery, custom shipping, catering or event planning). These may be Western Union, Zelle, Cash App or similar money transfer requests. Any 3rd party requests are often indicative of a scam. Please be aware that such payments are final. Likewise, do not issue refund requests via these payment methods. Use the original payment method provided by your customer.

If you face any of these red flags, we recommend some additional buyer verification checks. These can include a government-issued ID request, a telephone call, or a check via Zoom. Also, make sure that the order type you are handling correlates with your regular business practices. You always have an option to cancel the order and refund the initial payment if you spot behavior that may be considered fraudulent.

It’s also possible the buyer would try to abuse the chargeback mechanism and make a false claim.At Wix, we work hard to protect our merchants from fraudulent behavior. However you, as a merchant, are always the best line of defense against fraud, since you are fully aware of all that is happening with a particular order and buyer.In this article, learn about:

title: What happens after a visitor purchases a gift card using the Gift Card app on my Wix site?
content:
Q: What happens after a visitor purchases a gift card using the Gift Card app on my Wix site?
A: After visitors purchase gift cards using the Gift Card app, they see a confirmation message with the option to print the gift card. In addition, three emails are sent out:

* **Email to customer:** An email is sent to the buyer with the details of the purchase and an image of the card, which the buyer can print or forward by email. Tell your customers to check the spam folder if the email does not arrive. This email is sent from \[your email] via app-notifications.wix.com and has the subject line: Congratulations! You just purchased a gift card

* **Emails to you:**
  1. An email is sent to you (the site owner) containing information about the purchase, including the coupon code and "valid until" date. We advise you to keep this email so that when someone uses the gift card, you can verify the details. The email is sent from wix-team@app-notifications.wix.com and has the subject line: Someone just purchased a gift card from your website!
  2. A second email is sent which also included information about the purchase and contains a copy of the gift card. The email is sent from wix-team@app-notifications.wix.com and has the subject line: Copy of Gift Card ##\#\#-\#\#\#\#

Both you and the buyer can view details of the transaction in your PayPal accounts.

title: How can law enforcement agencies request personal information about a Wix user?
content:
Q: How can law enforcement agencies request personal information about a Wix user?
A: Law enforcement agencies can request personal information about a Wix user by obtaining a court order or subpoena. Wix is willing to cooperate with law enforcement agencies and share information after receiving such legal documents. The information is usually provided in hard copy to the address mentioned in the court order. All court orders or subpoenas should be sent to [subpoenas@wix.com](mailto:subpoenas@wix.com).

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/requesting-the-details-of-a-wix-user
evidence_json:
["Requesting the Details of a Wix User
https://support.wix.com/en/article/requesting-the-details-of-a-wix-user
Requesting the Details of a Wix User
User privacy is very important to us. Wix is not at liberty to provide personal information about our users, including email addresses, IP addresses etc.Having said this, as Wix.com is a public company, we are always willing to cooperate with law enforcement agencies and share information after receiving a court order or subpoena.If you are a member of a police department or government agency and are investigating an ongoing case, you may contact us at any time. Our policy is to comply as best as we can with any ongoing police investigations. We usually provide the information, in hard copy, to the address mentioned in the court order.If you are not a law enforcement officer and would like to have a site removed or obtain personally identifying information about a Wix user, you must obtain a court order, which we honor.We ask that all court orders or subpoenas be sent to subpoenas@wix.com.
For any additional questions regarding this matter, contact us and we will be happy to assist."]

title: Why is my Vimeo video not working on my Wix site after switching to Vimeo Plus?
content:
Q: Why is my Vimeo video not working on my Wix site after switching to Vimeo Plus?
A: If your Vimeo video is no longer working after switching to Vimeo Plus, Wix has changed the static domain from **static.wix.com** to **static.parastorage.com**. To resolve this issue, go to your Vimeo Plus settings and make sure that **static.parastorage.com** is defined as the allowed domain.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-editor-issues-with-vimeo-videos
evidence_json:
["Wix Editor: Issues With Vimeo Videos
https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-editor-issues-with-vimeo-videos

If you are experiencing a problem with your Vimeo video, please check the information below.
Vimeo Plus users: Wix has switched the static domain from static.wix.com to static.parastorage.com. Therefore, if your video is no longer working, go to your Vimeo Plus settings and make sure that static.parastorage.com is defined as the allowed domain.Note: Videos might not play automatically on iPhones/iPads as Apple blocks the autoplay function on their mobile devices. This is due to the fact that playing videos or music on a mobile device may incur additional data charges from the visitor's cellphone network. title: What are the different statuses a transaction can have in the Wix Payments table, and what do they mean?
content:
Q: What are the different statuses a transaction can have in the Wix Payments table, and what do they mean?
A: In the Wix Payments table, a transaction can have the following statuses:

- **Pending:** The transaction was approved, but the funds are not yet available for payout.
- **Successful:** The transaction was approved and the funds are available for payout.
- **Pending Refund:** The debit transaction (e.g. refund / chargeback) was approved, but the funds have not been debited from your account.
- **Refunded:** The debit transaction (e.g. refund / chargeback) was approved and funds were debited from your account.
- **Paid Out:** The transaction was included in a previous payout to your bank account.
- **Payout Reversed:** The transaction is part of a payout that was returned by your bank. The funds are available in your Wix Payments account.
- **Failed:** The transaction has failed.
- **Authorized:** The payment is approved by the customer’s payment method and the payment sum is held in their account, in readiness to be captured (paid) later.
- **Void:** The authorized payment is cancelled and the hold on the payment is released from your customer's account.
- **Suspicious:** There is a high probability that the order has been made without the cardholder’s knowledge or permission. Consider refunding the payment and holding off on fulfilling the order.
- **Action needed:** You received a chargeback and can choose whether to accept it or dispute it. You're still within the timeframe to submit the dispute.
- **Expires in "X" days:** You received a chargeback and can choose whether to accept it or dispute it. You have the indicated number of days to submit the dispute.
- **Expired:** The time frame for filing a dispute has passed. The chargeback's status is now final and cannot be changed.
- **Final:** You received a chargeback but cannot dispute it. This status cannot be changed.
- **Accepted:** You received a chargeback and accepted the claim. The funds remain with your customer.
- **Disputed:** You received a chargeback and filed a dispute against it. It is now in review by the relevant credit card issuer.
- **Lost:** The bank and the credit card issuer have reviewed your dispute and found your evidence insufficient to prove the charge is legitimate. The funds will remain with the customer, and you will not be able to dispute the decision through Wix Payments.
- **Won:** The bank and the credit card issuer have reviewed your dispute and decided to recognize the payment as a legitimate charge. The funds will return to your Wix Payments account along with the chargeback fee.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/understanding-your-wix-payments-transaction-table

title: Why am I not receiving verification SMS on my business phone number from services like Google or Facebook?
content:
Q: Why am I not receiving verification SMS on my business phone number from services like Google or Facebook?
A: When signing up for services such as Skype, Facebook, and Google, the company might send a verification SMS to the phone number you've provided in order to confirm your registration. Instead of using a regular 10 digit phone number, they send the SMS via a 'short code' or 5-6 digit number able to send and receive texts. Unfortunately, Business Phone Number cannot receive messages from these numbers. When signing up for a service like the examples above, we recommend using a phone number other than your business phone number as we cannot guarantee the verification message will go through.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/business-phone-number-issues-receiving-verification-sms

title: What are some of the advanced design features available in Editor X?
content:
Q: What are some of the advanced design features available in Editor X?
A: Editor X offers advanced design and layout capabilities that allow you to create complex website designs for any device, all without using code. Some of the features include:

- **Grid layouting**: An advanced two-dimensional layouting system based on CSS grid.
- **Docking**: Anchors elements to a specific position as the viewport changes.
- **Stack & scale media**: For seamless responsive behavior.
- **Text scale**: To create scalable font sizes.
- **Flex layouter**: A smart layouting system relying on flexbox technology for automatic reorganization of content while resizing.
- **Custom breakpoints**: To tailor designs to any viewport, not just classic devices.
- **Flexible canvas**: With resizing handles to instantly see and customize your design across viewports.
- **Advanced sizing control**: Defines your element as fixed or fluid, using wide support for modern CSS units.
- **Wix design system**: Featuring sections with built-in responsive behavior matched to the color palette of your site.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/introducing-editor-x

title: What should I do if my antivirus software flags a Wix site as unsafe?

title: How can I set up the Yelp app on my Wix site after adding it?
content:
Q: How can I set up the Yelp app on my Wix site after adding it?
A: ### To set up the Yelp app:

#### Step 1 | Open the Settings panel of the app
1. Select the app in the Editor.
2. Click **Settings**.

#### Step 2 | Connect your Yelp account
Click **Connect Account** and log in to your Yelp account or click **Create Account** to set up a new account.

#### Step 3 | Edit the app settings
1. Click the **Settings** tab.
2. Click the **Title Text** toggle: 
   * **Enabled**: A title appears in the Yelp app. Enter the title text.
   * **Disabled**: A title does not appear in the Yelp app.
3. Click the **Star Ratings** toggle: 
   * **Enabled**: Your review score appears in the Yelp app.
   * **Disabled**: Your review score does not appear in the Yelp app.
4. Click the **Reviews** toggle: 
   * **Enabled**: Your Yelp reviews appear in the app.
   * **Disabled**: Your Yelp reviews do not appear in the app.

#### Step 4 | Change the app layout
1. Click the **Layout** tab.
2. Choose the header layout.
3. Choose the layout of your star ratings.
4. Choose an option for reviewer profile images.

#### Step 5 | Customize the app design
1. Click the **Design** tab.
2. Click the color box to change the background color, and drag the slider to change the opacity.
3. Click the color box to change the border color and drag the slider to change the border width.
4. Click the color box to change the divider color and drag the slider to change the divider width.
5. Select a font style and color for each piece of text.

title: How does Wix handle pre-date charging for different services to ensure uninterrupted service?
content:
Q: How does Wix handle pre-date charging for different services to ensure uninterrupted service?
A: Wix attempts to process your renewal payment before your plan's expiry date to ensure there is no interruption to your service. Depending on your service or subscription, you may be charged on a monthly, annual, or 2-3 year basis. Here's how Wix's pre-date charging works:

* **Premium or Studio plans:**
  
  + **Monthly plans:** Same date as the expiry date
  + **Yearly plans:** 14 days prior to your plan's expiry date (anniversary of your purchase)
* **Third-party apps:** Same date as the expiry date
* **Domains:** 30 days prior to the expiry date
* **Business Emails:** 30 days prior to the expiry date

If the charge is unsuccessful, Wix attempts the transaction again to ensure continuity of service.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/understanding-how-wix-processes-payments-for-our-services

["Understanding How Wix Processes Payments for Our Services
https://support.wix.com/en/article/understanding-how-wix-processes-payments-for-our-services

Wix offers a range of billing and payment options to help you enjoy our premium services. When we charge for subscriptions, we may process your payment in a way to make it easier for you to manage your transactions and to ensure uninterrupted service to your site. You may see a single payment to Wix for multiple services, or be charged in advance of your renewal date. This article explains some of the different ways Wix processes your payments for Wix services.In this article, learn more about:

title: How can I view and chat with live site visitors using the Wix app?
content:
Q: How can I view and chat with live site visitors using the Wix app?
A: To view and chat with live site visitors using the Wix app, follow these steps:

1. Go to your site in the Wix app.
2. A notification appears at the top of the dashboard if you have live site visitors. Tap the notification to see the full list.
3. Site visitors appear as a number (Visitor #9504) if they are not registered to your site, or as their name if they are site members. To view more information about a visitor:
   - Tap the visitor you want to view.
   - Tap the drop-down next to **On Page** to view all the available details including the page of your site the visitor is currently on, the browser they're using, their location, and how many times they've previously visited.
4. You can also chat with any visitor in real-time. To chat with a visitor:

title: How can I ensure that my email marketing campaign has a clear and effective Call-To-Action (CTA)?
content:
Q: How can I ensure that my email marketing campaign has a clear and effective Call-To-Action (CTA)?
A: To ensure that your email marketing campaign has a clear and effective Call-To-Action (CTA), follow these guidelines:

* Avoid having too many CTAs as it can be distracting and prevent readers from focusing on your primary goal.
* If you do have multiple CTAs, limit them to three levels at most. Have a primary CTA that stands out, so it is obvious to your readers that it is the most important action. Then, include secondary CTAs, followed by the least important ones.
* Use buttons for the more important CTAs as they are more noticeable and attention-grabbing. Use links for the less important CTAs.
* If you have a lot of information to convey, it is better to link to a page on your site rather than including all of it in the email. Your email should act as a teaser or introduction.

By following these guidelines, you can make sure that your CTA is clear, focused, and effective.

Q: How can I view my Wix Analytics reports in different formats?
A: To view your data in a specific format in Wix Analytics reports, click an icon displayed next to a report:

- **Table** displays your data in rows and columns.
- **Bar Chart** displays and compares your data.
- **Line Chart** shows how your data has changed over time.
- **Map** displays geographical data.
- **Pie Chart** displays your data in sections.
- **Heat Map** displays your data using intensity of color in grid format.
- **Funnel** displays your data in steps.
- **Combo Chart and Bar Chart Split** display multiple data series in one report.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/about-wix-analytics-reports

title: How can customers redeem virtual gift cards at a Wix Mobile POS?
content:
Q: How can customers redeem virtual gift cards at a Wix Mobile POS?
A: When customers want to pay for their order using their gift card at your mobile POS, you need to select **Gift card** as the payment method. You can then enter the gift card code your customer received by email to redeem the card. If the value of the gift card doesn't cover the order, your customer can use any other payment method to pay for the balance.

title: How can I set up how customers earn points in my Wix Loyalty Program for my restaurant?
content:
Q: How can I set up how customers earn points in my Wix Loyalty Program for my restaurant?
A: Prerequisites: Ensure that you have updated your Restaurants Orders app to the latest version and created your loyalty program.

To set up how customers earn points:

1. Manage how customers earn points when they:
   * **Place a restaurant order:**
     1. Click **Edit Action** next to **Place a restaurant order**.
     2. Add a title to be shown on your live site.
     3. Choose how many points are earned per $1 spent.
     4. Click **Save**.
   * **Sign up to the site:**
     1. Click **Edit Action** next to **Sign up to the site**.
     2. Add a title to be shown on your live site.
     3. Choose how many points are earned per $1 spent.
     4. Click **Save**.
2. Click **Next**.

title: What actions do I need to take to comply with the EU Consumer Rights Directive 2014 for my Wix Store?
content:
Q: What actions do I need to take to comply with the EU Consumer Rights Directive 2014 for my Wix Store?
A: To comply with the EU Consumer Rights Directive 2014 for your Wix Store, you need to take the following actions:

- **State the return policy on your site**: EU customers have 14 calendar days from the purchase date to return items for any reason. You can simply state this on your site.

- **Refund customers within 14 days of cancellation**: From the day of cancellation, you have 14 days to refund your customer. You can refund customers through your payment method.

- **Show the total cost of the purchase**: The Wix Stores format already includes this, so no action is required.

- **State who will be responsible for the cost of returning items**: At the time of sale, clearly state who will be responsible for the cost of returning items. You can simply state this on your site.

- **Provide a withdrawal form**: Add a contact form and customize it as a withdrawal form for canceling contracts and initiating returns.

- **Remove all pre-ticked boxes**: Ensure there are no pre-ticked boxes on your website that offer consumers extra services. No action is required if this is already the case.

Please note that this information is not legal advice. Consult with a legal professional for further information.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-stores-impact-of-eu-directive-concerning-online-businesses

title: Is there a feature that allows returning to the last-visited page of a pagination bar when moving between pages?
content:
Q: Is there a feature that allows returning to the last-visited page of a pagination bar when moving between pages?
A: Currently, when a site visitor goes to a page that includes a pagination bar, they are always brought to page 1. This happens regardless of what page the visitor came from. For example, if a visitor clicks page 3 of the pagination bar and then clicks one of the items to open that item page, when they click 'back' from the item page, they get brought to page 1 of the dynamic list page, even though they had last been on page 3.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/cms-request-returning-to-the-last-visited-page-of-a-pagination-bar-when-moving-between-pages
evidence_json:
["CMS Request: Returning to the Last-Visited Page of a Pagination Bar When Moving Between Pages
https://support.wix.com/en/article/cms-request-returning-to-the-last-visited-page-of-a-pagination-bar-when-moving-between-pages
CMS Request: Returning to the Last-Visited Page of a Pagination Bar When Moving Between Pages
Currently, when a site visitor goes to a page that includes a pagination bar, they are always brought to page 1. This happens regardless of what page the visitor came from.Take, for example, a site that has a dynamic list page with a repeater to display collection items. This page includes a pagination bar, so visitors can see more collection items on more pages.A visitor clicks page 3 of the pagination bar, and then clicks one of the items to open that item page. When they click 'back' from the item page, they get brought to page 1 of the dynamic list page. This happens even though they had last been on page 3 of the dynamic list page.We are always working to update and improve our products, and your feedback is hugely appreciated."]

title: What are the Core Web Vitals metrics included in Google's assessment, and what do they measure?
content:
Q: What are the Core Web Vitals metrics included in Google's assessment, and what do they measure?
A: Google's Core Web Vitals Assessment includes the following metrics:

- **Largest Contentful Paint (LCP):** An indication of a site's loading time, specifically how long it takes for the largest content element in the site's viewport to load.
- **Interaction to Next Paint (INP):** An assessment of your site's responsiveness to all click, tap, and keyboard interactions that occur throughout each visit on every page. The final INP value is the longest interaction observed.
- **Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS):** A measurement of unexpected movements of elements that change the layout of the page.

title: How can I adjust my live stream settings in OBS Studio to ensure optimal performance with Wix Video?
content:
Q: How can I adjust my live stream settings in OBS Studio to ensure optimal performance with Wix Video?
A: To adjust your live stream settings in OBS Studio for optimal performance with Wix Video, follow these steps:

1. Open the OBS Studio Encoder on your computer.
2. Click **Settings** on the bottom right.
3. Select the **Output** tab to change the codec, audio, and video bitrates.
4. Select the **Video** tab to change the video resolution.

Make sure you don't exceed the following settings:
- **Video Resolution:** 720p (1280x720)
- **Codec:** x264
- **Video bitrate:** ~2500 kbps
- **Audio bitrate:** AAC 44.1kHz ~128kbps

title: What should I do if I receive a 403 error message in Google Search Console for a URL on my site?
content:
Q: What should I do if I receive a 403 error message in Google Search Console for a URL on my site?
A: If you receive a 403 error message for a URL, you should review the list of your site pages to check that no pages were restricted by mistake with passwords or with member-only restrictions. This error message is nothing to worry about, as it does not harm your site's SEO and the only outcome is that the restricted pages are not indexed by Google.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/google-search-console-403-error
evidence_json:

https://support.wix.com/en/article/google-search-console-403-error
Google Search Console: 403 Error
If you have password protected a page on your site, or set a page as member-only, Google will get a 403 response (forbidden) and log it under Crawl Errors. 
This error message is nothing to worry about, Google is just alerting you that there are pages on your site that are restricted. This error does not harm your site's SEO and the only outcome is that the restricted pages are not indexed by Google.If you receive a 403 error message for a URL you should review the list of your site pages to check that no pages were restricted by mistake with passwords or with member-only restrictions. "]

- Make sure that your logo looks good in all sizes, from large to small. Try to zoom out or check it in a small size like it normally appears on your brand materials, and check that everything is clear, and the text is readable.
- Avoid overlapping text when designing your logo, as the texts blend into one color and are unreadable in some files. This happens in the following file types:

Additionally, ensure that the elements contrast against their background to prevent them from looking pixelated in small sizes. Be cautious with extremely thin font weights or thin-lined icons and shapes, as they can look blurred or even invisible in small sizes.

title: What are the requirements for uploading a photo ID for Wix Payments verification?
content:
Q: What are the requirements for uploading a photo ID for Wix Payments verification?
A: Your photo ID must meet the following requirements:

* Your photo ID can be a passport, driver's license or a government issued ID card
* Your photo ID must be active and non-expired
* The photo must be in color
* Your ID must show all 4 borders and corners
* The ID must not have information blocked or blacked out
* The ID must be straightened, not angled or rotated
* The ID must not be blurry, overexposed or copied from another source (e.g. screenshot)
* Your first, middle and last name in your Wix Payments account must match those of your ID
* Your birth date in your Wix Payments account must match that of your ID
* For passports with a Machine-Readable Zone (MRZ), the MRZ must be visible.
* For driver's licenses or government issue ID cards, send a separate file for each side
* Documents must be sent in one of the following: HEIC, JPEG, JPG, PDF, PNG
* The maximum file size is 10 MB
* The minimum file size is 1 KB for PDF, 100 KB for other formats

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/guidelines-for-uploading-documentation-for-wix-payments

- **Top selling variants (Wix Stores):** Discover which product variants (e.g., size L, color brown) are selling the most.
- **Most abandoned products (Wix Stores):** Understand which products visitors add to their cart but don't end up purchasing.
- **Most booked services (Wix Bookings):** Discover which services were booked the most.
- **Top paying subscriptions (Wix Pricing Plans):** See which subscriptions bring you the most revenue.
- **Top selling events (Wix Events):** Discover which events bring you the most revenue and see the total tickets sold for each event.
- **Top selling dishes (Wix Restaurants):** See your top selling dishes and find out what customers ordered the most.

These metrics vary depending on your business app. For example, if you've installed Wix Events, you will see 'Tickets sold' as a top stat.

title: How can I view the predicted occupancy for my classes in Wix Analytics?
content:
Q: How can I view the predicted occupancy for my classes in Wix Analytics?
A: To view the predicted occupancy for your classes in Wix Analytics, follow these steps:

1. Go to the **Bookings Overview** page in the **Overviews** section under **Analytics** in your site's dashboard.
2. Choose the **Classes** view at the top right according to your service type.
3. In the **Predicted occupancy** section, click the drop-down to show the predicted occupancy for the **next week** (7 days starting next Sunday) or the **next 7 days** (7 days starting tomorrow).
4. The progress bar will show you the following details:
   - **Spots filled/Confirmed appointments:** This is the number of already booked sessions.
   - **Predicted:** This is the number of additional bookings that are likely to be made based on the confirmed bookings from the previous 3-4 weeks.
   - **Available:** This is the number of spots left open, calculated as the total capacity minus predicted occupancy.

**Note:** Predicted occupancy is the sum of confirmed spots that you already have for the next week/next 7 days and the predicted spots. The predicted numbers rely on the number of confirmed bookings in the past 3-4 weeks.

content:
Q: How can I set up and customize the display of a single event using Wix Events in ADI?
A: Prerequisites: Ensure that you have already added the Wix Events app to your site.

To set up and customize the display of a single event:

1. Click the Event section on your site.
2. Select an event to display from the drop-down on the left.
3. Customize your section using the options below:
   * **RSVP Button Text:** Personalize the button.
   * **RSVP Title:** Select or deselect the checkbox to add or remove the text that appears above your button.
   * **Display Details:** Select or deselect the checkboxes to display or hide different elements.
   * **Image Scaling:** Click the drop-down menu and select an option:
     + **Fit:** Fit and display the entire image in the image space of your section.
     + **Crop:** Crop the image to fit the entire image space of your section.

title: What happens to my Google Ads credits if I pause a campaign using Wix?
content:
Q: What happens to my Google Ads credits if I pause a campaign using Wix?
A: If you pause a campaign, you have the option at any time to resume the campaign using only your remaining Google ad credits. As soon as you pause, the following changes happen:

* Your ad is no longer shown on Google.
* Your remaining ad credits remain in your account.
* If the paused campaign was your last active campaign on the account, auto renew is turned off for the subscription.

**Note:** Any Google Ads credits that have an expiry date may expire while the campaign is paused.

title: What is the purpose of TTL in DNS records and should I change the default TTL value?
content:
Q: What is the purpose of TTL in DNS records and should I change the default TTL value?
A: Time to live (TTL) is the value of time that tells servers how long to store a DNS record locally before discarding. You should leave the TTL for your DNS records set to the default time. Changing a TTL value does not speed up the time it takes for a DNS record to propagate. It only changes the amount of time before your computer is forced to make a new DNS request.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/about-ttl

title: Why does a charge appear twice on my customer's bank statement, and what should be done if it doesn't disappear?
content:
Q: Why does a charge appear twice on my customer's bank statement, and what should be done if it doesn't disappear?
A: Sometimes a charge may appear to have been made twice on your customer's bank statement. This does not mean that your customer makes two payments. When paying for goods or services by credit card, a credit card company may authorize the card for the amount due before the actual funds are taken. The authorization (pending charge) appears on your customer's bank statement and may look like a charge, however, no funds are actually taken at that time. The authorization should disappear from online bank statements within a month. If the authorization does not disappear, please advise your customer to contact their bank for further information.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/understanding-double-charges-on-your-customers-bank-statements
evidence_json:
["Understanding Double Charges on Your Customers' Bank Statements
https://support.wix.com/en/article/understanding-double-charges-on-your-customers-bank-statements
Understanding Double Charges on Your Customers' Bank Statements
Sometimes a charge may appear to have been made twice on your customer's bank statement. title: How can I ensure that using Google Fonts on my Wix site complies with the GDPR?
content:
Q: How can I ensure that using Google Fonts on my Wix site complies with the GDPR?
A: In a recent decision, a regional court in Munich ruled that the “dynamic use” of Google Fonts violates the EU GDPR. This is due to the fact that your visitor's IP address could be transmitted to Google's servers in the United States. Wix has developed an in-house solution to remedy this issue. Google Fonts are now hosted locally within Wix. This means that no IP data is transmitted from the EU to Google's servers in the United States. 

**Note**: If you add fonts to your site using alternative methods such as custom embeds, custom elements or iframes, they may contain Google Fonts and we cannot guarantee that these will be hosted locally.

title: How can I view the revenue from different types of subscriptions over the last 12 months in Wix Analytics?
content:
Q: How can I view the revenue from different types of subscriptions over the last 12 months in Wix Analytics?
A: To view the revenue from different types of subscriptions over the last 12 months in Wix Analytics, go to the **Revenue over the last 12 months** section. This section displays a graph of the total revenue you've received from different types of subscriptions on your site over the last 12 months. You can view revenue for all plans together or click the **All plans** drop-down to filter by a specific plan. The 4 revenue types include:

* **One-time:** Revenue from subscriptions that aren’t recurring (the client pays only once).
* **First recurring:** Revenue from the first payment of a recurring subscription.
* **Recurring:** Revenue from recurring payments (excluding first payment).
* **Expected recurring:** This metric calculates all the payments that you should get from existing subscriptions this month, but have not yet received.

**Important:** This isn’t a prediction based on historical sales, rather a projection of upcoming payments for existing subscriptions. This metric does not include new subscriptions that may be purchased in the future (during this month), and does not consider any possible cancellations.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-analytics-about-the-subscriptions-overview

title: What are the supported file types and size limits for uploading images to a Wix site?
content:
Q: What are the supported file types and size limits for uploading images to a Wix site?
A: For site images, Wix supports the following file types: JPG, PNG, GIF, JPEG, JPE, JFIF, BMP, HEIC, HEIF, TIFF, TIF, WEBP, JPEG 2000, and RAW. The supported JPEG 2000 file formats include .jp2, .jpg2, .j2k, .jpf, .jpm, .j2c, .jpc, .jpx, and the supported RAW file formats include .arw, .srw, .nef, .cr2, .cr3, .crw, .rwl, .rw2, .raw, .raf, .pef, .orf, .mrw, .dng, .sr2, .srf, .kdc, .k25, .dcr, .x3f, .erf, .3fr. Animated WEBP images are currently not supported and convert to static images.

The file size limits for images are 25MB, and for GIFs, it is 15MB.

For background images, the supported file types are JPG, PNG, GIF, JPEG, JPE, JFIF, BMP, HEIC, HEIF, TIFF, TIF, and WEBP, with a recommended file size of at least 3000 x 3000px.

title: How can I enable Single Sign-On (SSO) login for my organization using Wix?
content:
Q: How can I enable Single Sign-On (SSO) login for my organization using Wix?
A: Prerequisites: Ensure you have completed the setup of your Identity Provider (IdP) settings and have the necessary information such as Client ID, Client Secret, and Config URL.

To enable SSO login and set it as required:

1. Click the **Enable SSO** toggle to enable or disable SSO login:
   * **Enabled:** Your users can sign in to their Wix account using SSO or other methods such as an email address and password.
   * **Disabled:** Your users cannot sign in using SSO. They can still sign in using other methods.
2. Click the **Set SSO as required** toggle to choose whether or not you want to require your users to sign in by SSO.
   * **Enabled:** Users can only sign in with SSO. They cannot sign in using other methods such as an email and password. Account owners can still sign in using other methods.
   * **Disabled:** Users can sign in using SSO or other methods.

**Important:** Wix recommends that you manually test your SSO settings before setting SSO as required.

3. Click **Save Changes**.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-enterprise-setting-up-single-sign-on-sso-login

title: How does Wix optimize image loading to improve site performance?
content:
Q: How does Wix optimize image loading to improve site performance?
A: Wix optimizes image loading through automatic image optimization and lazy loading. When you upload an image to a Wix site, images less than 25MB are automatically compressed for optimal quality and site loading time. Additionally, Wix uses a technique called lazy loading, which boosts loading time by replacing high-resolution images with low-resolution versions. The low-resolution placeholders load instantly, while the high-resolution content loads in the background and automatically replaces the placeholders once loaded.

title: How can I view the individual recipient statistics for my email campaign in the Wix app?
content:
Q: How can I view the individual recipient statistics for my email campaign in the Wix app?
A: In the Wix app, you can view the individual recipient statistics for your email campaign by accessing the **Recipient Stats** section. This section provides a breakdown of the following metrics:

- **Sent:** The total amount of contacts you've sent the email campaign to.
- **Delivered:** The total number of contacts who received your email campaign to their inboxes. You can also see the percentage they make of those sent.
- **Opened:** The contacts who have opened your email campaign. You can also see the percentage they make of those delivered.
- **Clicked:** The contacts who have clicked links inside your email campaign (a button, a direct URL). You can also see the percentage they make of those opened.
- **Not delivered:** The total number of contacts who did not receive your email campaign because these emails bounced.
- **Not opened:** The contacts who received the campaign but did not open it.

**Tip:** Click any stat to see the list of recipients that were counted.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/email-marketing-understanding-your-campaign-statistics-in-the-wix-owner-app
evidence_json:
["Email Marketing: Understanding Your Campaign Statistics in the Wix App
https://support.wix.com/en/article/email-marketing-understanding-your-campaign-statistics-in-the-wix-owner-app
Email Marketing: Understanding Your Campaign Statistics in the Wix App
Using the Wix app, you can keep track of your email campaigns and analyze their performance on the go. Get an overview of all your campaigns at once from the main dashboard and click a specific campaign to see more details.Recipient StatsRecipient Stats are the individual stats for each recipient you sent the email campaign to. In this section, each contact is counted once even if they took the action multiple times. For example, if the same person has opened your email three times, they will still be counted as one.  
Sent: The total amount of contacts you've sent the email campaign to.  Delivered: The total number of contacts who received your email campaign to their inboxes.

title: How can I ensure that a form in Wix CMS does not submit if a required field is left empty?
content:
Q: How can I ensure that a form in Wix CMS does not submit if a required field is left empty?
A: Most input elements can be set as "Required." When an input element is required, the form will not submit if the field is empty. This prevents incomplete submissions and ensures that all necessary information is collected. If you set the connected collection field to "Required," users will see an error message if they attempt to submit the form with empty values. Note that switches do not have a "Required" option, but checkboxes do.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/cms-about-validation-settings-for-input-elements

Wix's Content Management System (CMS) allows you to create custom forms with input elements that submit to your collection. Using the validation settings in your input elements helps ensure that the data you collect from visitors meets your specific requirements. You can also set validations for the collection fields that store the submitted input values.Using validation settings for input elements in your Wix CMS ensures that the data collected is accurate, complete, and meets your specific requirements.
